name: Single-system multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of CD1a+ and/or Langerin (CD207)+ Langerhans cells on biopsy
Radiologic evidence of multifocal bone lesions confined to a single system
Clinical presentation consistent with LCH including localized bone pain or swelling

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation plus radiologic evidence of multifocal lesions within a single system
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of multisystem involvement is essential to classify as single-system multifocal LCH.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lytic bone lesions with beveled edges
searchTerms: holes in bone with sharp edges
Langerhans cell infiltration confirmed by biopsy
specific immune cells found in biopsy

common.symptomName: Soft tissue swelling over affected bone
Limited range of motion near affected skeletal sites

searchTerms: lymph node swelling adjacent to bone

occasional.symptomName: Skin rash localized near bone lesions

rare.symptomName: Diabetes insipidus due to pituitary involvement
searchTerms: excessive thirst and urination from pituitary damage
diabetes insipidus symptoms due to pituitary problems
inability to concentrate urine causing dehydration

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms from adjacent CNS involvement
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from nearby brain involvement

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated liver function tests
imaging: Multiple lytic bone lesions with well-defined beveled edges on X-ray
MRI showing marrow infiltration without soft tissue mass
Bone scintigraphy demonstrating multifocal skeletal uptake
genetic: Somatic BRAF V600E mutation in lesional Langerhans cells in approximately 50% of cases
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a and Langerin (CD207)
Electron microscopy showing Birbeck granules in Langerhans cells

distinguishingFeatures: Eosinophilic granuloma is a unifocal bone lesion rather than multifocal
Non-infectious inflammatory bone lesions without Langerhans cell infiltration

redFlags: Rapid progression of bone lesions with neurological deficits
Development of diabetes insipidus or other endocrine dysfunction
Signs of multisystem involvement such as hepatosplenomegaly or cytopenias
references: Aricò M, et al. Langerhans cell histiocytosis in adults. Eur J Cancer. 2003.
Allen CE, et al. Langerhans cell histiocytosis: emerging insights and clinical implications. Blood. 2015.
Gadner H, et al. Langerhans cell histiocytosis: consensus recommendations for diagnosis, clinical work-up, and treatment. Pediatr Blood Cancer. 2013.
